one_liner: Point-prompt jitter variance of SAM masks predicts human inter-annotator disagreement per object.
problem: SAM outputs change under tiny prompt displacements, but nobody has established what this instability measures. It is treated as a nuisance rather than a signal.
core_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: the variance of SAM masks under small point jitter (e.g. 5-15 px perturbations) correlates strongly (rank r>0.6) with human inter-annotator mask disagreement on the same object, i.e. prompt sensitivity is an intrinsic object-ambiguity meter, not model noise.
why_important: Would give a free, model-based ambiguity estimator usable for annotation routing, QA, and uncertainty without any labels.
why_possibly_novel: Prompt sensitivity is usually reported as a robustness defect; recasting it as a calibrated measurement of stimulus ambiguity is a different scientific claim. UNVERIFIED - needs lit search.
minimal_experiment: Take a multi-annotator dataset (e.g. LVIS double annotations or a multi-rater medical set), compute SAM jitter-variance per object, correlate with inter-rater IoU. One GPU-day.
main_risk: Correlation may be driven trivially by object size or boundary length; must partial these out.

one_liner: Test whether SAM's three ambiguity heads implement a stable part/object/group hierarchy or an arbitrary mode split.
problem: SAM returns 3 masks for ambiguous prompts. The community assumes they represent whole/part/subpart levels, but this has not been verified across categories.
core_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: the identity of each output head is not semantically stable; head-to-granularity assignment flips across categories and even across prompt positions within one object, refuting the implicit 'hierarchy heads' assumption.
why_important: Many pipelines pick a fixed head or trust head order; if assignment is unstable, those pipelines have a silent failure mode.
why_possibly_novel: Papers use the multimask output constantly but rarely audit what each head means. UNVERIFIED - needs lit search.
minimal_experiment: For 1k objects with part annotations (PartImageNet, PACO), classify each head output as part/object/group by IoU and measure head-assignment consistency statistics.
main_risk: Result may be 'mostly stable', a weaker but still publishable calibration finding.

one_liner: SAM thin-structure failure is caused by patch-grid aliasing, not decoder capacity.
problem: SAM notoriously breaks wires, poles, and thin legs. The default explanation is decoder capacity or training data, but thin structures alias against the 16-px patch grid.
core_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: for structures thinner than ~1 patch, SAM mask quality is a strong function of the structure's sub-patch phase and orientation relative to the tokenization grid; phase-averaging inputs (sub-patch shifts) recovers a large fraction of the error without any retraining.
why_important: Locates the failure in tokenization physics rather than learning, which changes what fixes are rational.
why_possibly_novel: Aliasing analyses exist for CNN downsampling (KNOWN: Zhang, 'Making Convolutional Networks Shift-Invariant Again'), but a phase-sweep causal study on promptable ViT segmenters is UNVERIFIED - needs lit search.
minimal_experiment: Render synthetic bars of controlled width/orientation, sweep sub-pixel translation, plot SAM IoU vs phase; then test phase-jitter ensembling on real wire/pole classes.
main_risk: Failure may be dominated by training-data scarcity of thin objects, with aliasing a minor term.

one_liner: Box prompts act as scale priors that override image evidence when box and object conflict.
problem: Box-prompted SAM is assumed to segment 'the object in the box', but boxes also carry scale/aspect information the model may trust more than pixels.
core_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: when a box is systematically inflated or squashed (e.g. 1.5x width), SAM's mask follows the box geometry rather than the true object boundary in a predictable, measurable way (mask aspect regresses toward box aspect), demonstrating that boxes are priors, not just localizers.
why_important: Auto-labeling pipelines feed detector boxes into SAM; detector box errors would then be copied into masks, correlated and invisible.
why_possibly_novel: Box-perturbation robustness is reported as a scalar; the directional 'mask follows box geometry' regression law is unquantified. UNVERIFIED - needs lit search.
minimal_experiment: On COCO GT boxes, apply controlled aspect/scale perturbations, fit mask-aspect vs box-aspect response curves per category.
main_risk: Effect may be small for well-textured objects and only matter for low-contrast ones; need stratified analysis.

one_liner: Negative clicks carve masks asymmetrically: exclusion near boundaries works, exclusion inside homogeneous regions fails.
problem: Interactive SAM correction assumes positive and negative clicks are symmetric information. Practitioners observe negatives often do nothing or overshoot.
core_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: the information gain of a negative click is a strong function of local feature contrast: negatives placed in feature-homogeneous regions (same texture as the object) reduce error far less per click than positives of matched placement, making click budgets asymmetric.
why_important: Click-budget benchmarks (NoC) average over this; interfaces could route users toward the click type with higher expected gain.
why_possibly_novel: Click simulators treat clicks symmetrically; a measured positive/negative information asymmetry law would be new. UNVERIFIED - needs lit search.
minimal_experiment: On DAVIS/COCO objects, exhaustively grid-place a single corrective negative vs positive click, map per-pixel error reduction, compare distributions.
main_risk: Asymmetry might be an artifact of one model version; verify on SAM-HQ and SAM2 image mode.

one_liner: SAM snaps to luminance edges even when the semantic boundary is texture- or material-defined; quantify the edge-snapping bias.
problem: SAM boundaries look crisp, but crispness may come from locking onto intensity gradients rather than the true semantic boundary (e.g. shadow edges, printed patterns).
core_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: on stimuli where the semantic boundary and the strongest local intensity edge are deliberately separated (shadow crossing an object, texture-defined figure), SAM boundary placement is biased toward the intensity edge by a measurable offset that scales with edge contrast ratio.
why_important: Explains a family of confident-but-wrong boundaries (shadow inclusion, pattern following) that boundary metrics currently lump into generic error.
why_possibly_novel: Edge-snapping is folklore; a psychophysics-style controlled quantification with synthesized conflict stimuli appears missing. UNVERIFIED - needs lit search.
minimal_experiment: Composite objects with controllable shadow/texture edges (cut-and-paste with relighting), sweep contrast, measure boundary displacement toward distractor edge.
main_risk: Synthetic conflict stimuli may be out-of-distribution in ways that exaggerate the bias.

one_liner: SAM's predicted-IoU head is miscalibrated in a shape-dependent way: overconfident on concave and perforated objects.
problem: Predicted IoU is widely used to filter auto-generated masks (SA-1B itself was built this way), but its calibration as a function of object geometry is unexamined.
core_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: predicted-IoU error is systematically structured by shape statistics (convexity, genus, boundary tortuosity): calibration is good for convex blobs and degrades monotonically with concavity/holes, so IoU-filtered datasets are silently biased toward simple shapes.
why_important: If true, every dataset distilled through SAM confidence filtering under-represents complex shapes, and models trained on them inherit a simplicity prior - a compounding ecosystem bias.
why_possibly_novel: Connects mask-confidence calibration to dataset evolution/inbreeding; per-geometry calibration audits of SAM are UNVERIFIED - needs lit search.
minimal_experiment: On COCO/ADE GT, bin objects by convexity and genus, plot predicted vs actual IoU per bin; then measure shape statistics of SA-1B vs a human-annotated reference.
main_risk: SA-1B shape bias could stem from its prompting grid rather than the IoU filter; needs an ablation to attribute.

one_liner: Iterative click sequences are path-dependent: the same click set in different orders yields different SAM masks.
problem: Interactive segmentation evaluation assumes the final mask depends on the set of corrections, but SAM conditions on previous mask state, making the process a dynamical system.
core_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: permuting the order of an identical set of 4-6 clicks changes final mask IoU by a nontrivial margin (>5 IoU on ambiguous objects), and there exist 'trap' orders from which no small click set recovers - i.e. interactive SAM has attractor states.
why_important: Path dependence means NoC benchmarks measure simulator policy as much as model quality, and real users can get stuck through no fault of their own.
why_possibly_novel: Framing interactive segmentation as a dynamical system with attractors and measuring order effects is not standard. UNVERIFIED - needs lit search.
minimal_experiment: Sample 200 hard objects, enumerate permutations of a fixed 4-click set, report IoU dispersion and identify absorbing bad states.
main_risk: Effect may vanish on easy objects, limiting scope to the ambiguous tail (which is arguably where it matters).

one_liner: Predict SAM failure before decoding from encoder attention statistics alone.
problem: Failure detection for SAM currently uses output-side signals (predicted IoU, stability score). Whether failure is already legible in the encoder is unknown.
core_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: a linear probe on encoder attention-map statistics (entropy, sink mass, head disagreement) at the prompt location predicts mask failure (IoU<0.5) with AUROC>0.8, i.e. most failures are encoder-representation failures, not decoder mistakes.
why_important: Locates the failure stage (representation vs readout), and gives a cheap abort/route-to-human signal that does not require running multiple decodes.
why_possibly_novel: Stage-attribution of promptable segmentation failures is largely unexplored. UNVERIFIED - needs lit search.
minimal_experiment: Log encoder statistics + outcome over 20k prompts on 3 datasets, train the probe, compare AUROC vs predicted-IoU baseline.
main_risk: Probe may just re-learn object size/contrast correlates of difficulty rather than model-internal evidence.

one_liner: SAM merges instances of periodic textures (fences, railings, book spines) when spatial period is below token resolution.
problem: Repeated near-identical instances are a known annoyance, but the quantitative relationship between texture period and instance-merging has not been mapped.
core_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: instance-level prompting accuracy on periodic arrays collapses sharply when the array period drops below ~2 patch widths, and the collapse point shifts predictably with input resolution - a measurable 'instance Nyquist limit'.
why_important: Defines a hard operating boundary for promptable segmentation in retail, agriculture (crop rows), and document images, and predicts exactly when zooming will fix it.
why_possibly_novel: A Nyquist-style law for instance separability in promptable models is a crisper claim than 'small objects are hard'. UNVERIFIED - needs lit search.
minimal_experiment: Procedurally render object arrays with controlled period/count, prompt the center instance, plot single-instance IoU vs period/patch ratio across resolutions.
main_risk: Real scenes add occlusion and perspective; the clean law may blur in the wild.

one_liner: Sub-patch objects get quantized to the token grid: measure the staircase floor of SAM on <16 px objects.
problem: SAM small-object failure is usually attributed to semantics or data. A simpler mechanical explanation: masks cannot express detail below feature-map resolution regardless of semantics.
core_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: for objects below ~16 px, SAM's best-achievable IoU (even with oracle prompts and oracle head choice) is bounded by a resolution floor computable from the mask-decoder upsampling path, and observed errors match this floor - meaning small-object failure is mostly resolution, not recognition.
why_important: Separates 'model cannot see it' from 'model cannot draw it'; the fix differs completely (zoom pipelines vs retraining).
why_possibly_novel: An explicit computed-vs-observed error floor comparison for promptable segmenters is missing. UNVERIFIED - needs lit search.
minimal_experiment: Take objects at many scales, segment at native + digitally zoomed resolution, compare the error decomposition against the theoretical decoder floor.
main_risk: Decoder nonlinearity may make the 'theoretical floor' hard to define cleanly; may need an empirical oracle-upsampler proxy.

one_liner: Cluster SAM's mask-token embeddings across millions of prompts to test whether text-free training induced a latent semantic taxonomy.
problem: SAM was trained without labels. Whether its object-level tokens organize into semantic structure (animal vs artifact, etc.) or purely geometric structure is an open representational question.
core_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: mask-token embeddings cluster by geometry (shape, size, texture) and NOT by semantic category - i.e. semantic clustering accuracy will be near chance once shape covariates are controlled, contradicting casual claims that 'SAM knows objects'.
why_important: Clarifies what class-agnostic pretraining actually learns, informing when SAM features can and cannot substitute for semantic backbones.
why_possibly_novel: Controlled geometry-vs-semantics decomposition of SAM token space (with shape covariates regressed out) is UNVERIFIED - needs lit search.
minimal_experiment: Extract mask tokens for 50k labeled COCO/ADE objects, run category linear probe before/after regressing out shape descriptors; compare with a CLIP-feature control.
main_risk: Shape and semantics are naturally confounded; the covariate control must be convincing.

one_liner: Define 'prompt compressibility' - the minimum click set reproducing a GT mask - as a measurable object complexity scale.
problem: There is no principled per-object measure of how hard an object is for promptable segmentation; NoC conflates simulator policy with intrinsic difficulty.
core_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: the minimal sufficient prompt set size (found by search, not by a fixed simulator) forms a stable complexity measure that (a) is consistent across SAM variants and (b) predicts real human annotation time better than object area, boundary length, or NoC from standard simulators.
why_important: Would give datasets an intrinsic difficulty axis and annotation-cost predictor, useful for budgeting and curriculum design.
why_possibly_novel: Kolmogorov-style 'description length in clicks' framing of segmentation difficulty appears new. UNVERIFIED - needs lit search.
minimal_experiment: Beam-search minimal click sets on 500 objects, correlate with logged human annotation times (e.g. from an internal labeling session).
main_risk: Search cost per object; and minimality may be model-specific despite the cross-variant claim.

one_liner: Map the phase diagram of prompt positions that flip SAM mask topology - the 'topological instability atlas' of an image.
problem: Some single-pixel prompt moves cause categorical mask changes (object vs part vs background leak). Where these cliff edges live and what image structure creates them is uncharacterized.
core_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: topology-flip boundaries in prompt space concentrate along medial-axis and low-contrast corridors of the underlying objects, so the instability atlas is predictable from image structure without running SAM densely.
why_important: Predictable instability zones let interfaces warn users, let simulators sample fairly, and reveal what the decoder's implicit object model is.
why_possibly_novel: Dense prompt-space mapping exists in robustness papers as averages; structural prediction of instability geography is UNVERIFIED - needs lit search.
minimal_experiment: Densely evaluate prompts on 100 images, compute flip boundaries, test prediction from medial axis + local contrast features.
main_risk: Atlas may be high-frequency noise rather than structured, making prediction fail (itself an informative negative).

one_liner: Attribute SAM small-object errors to resolution vs recognition with a zoom-oracle: how much failure survives perfect zoom?
problem: Zoom-in cascades are the standard small-object fix, but nobody has cleanly measured what fraction of failure is unfixable by resolution alone.
core_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: with an oracle crop centered on each small object at optimal zoom, SAM recovers >70% of the IoU gap on natural images, but a hard residual remains concentrated in low-contrast and cluttered contexts where recognition, not resolution, is the limit.
why_important: Quantifies the ceiling of all zoom-based engineering fixes and identifies the residual scientific problem.
why_possibly_novel: The oracle-zoom decomposition, reported per failure type, is a cleaner attribution than existing multi-scale ablations. UNVERIFIED - needs lit search.
minimal_experiment: On LVIS-small and xView-like imagery, run SAM native vs oracle-crop, decompose the gap by contrast/clutter strata.
main_risk: Oracle crops change context available to the model, conflating context loss with resolution gain; needs padded-crop controls.

one_liner: SAM draws sharper boundaries than humans do on intrinsically fuzzy objects - measure the sharpness mismatch distribution.
problem: On hair, fur, foliage, and smoke-like regions, ground truth is soft but SAM outputs hard crisp curves. The statistical mismatch between model boundary sharpness and human boundary width is undocumented.
core_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: SAM's boundary transition width is near-constant (a decoder property) regardless of the stimulus' physical edge width, whereas human annotations widen with stimulus fuzziness - so a single scalar 'sharpness mismatch' per class predicts where SAM boundary metrics are meaningless.
why_important: Identifies where binary mask evaluation stops being well-posed and matting-style evaluation must take over.
why_possibly_novel: Boundary-width statistics as a function of stimulus edge width, compared human-vs-model, appears unmeasured. UNVERIFIED - needs lit search.
minimal_experiment: Estimate edge transition widths from alpha mattes (Adobe matting datasets), compare with SAM logit transition widths per stimulus.
main_risk: Logit sharpness may be an artifact of the final threshold rather than the representation; inspect pre-threshold logits.

one_liner: SA-1B's auto-mask pipeline imprinted a closed-compact-region prior on SAM; open curves and wiry objects are structurally outside its output space.
problem: SAM fails on wires, cracks, and open contours. This is usually attributed to rarity, but SA-1B's generation process (grid prompts + IoU filtering) may have structurally excluded non-blob masks.
core_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: the shape-statistics gap between SA-1B masks and a reference human-annotated distribution (elongation, genus, solidity tails) quantitatively predicts SAM's per-shape-class failure rates - data-generating-process bias, not visual difficulty, explains wiry-object failure.
why_important: Reframes a famous failure mode as an auditable dataset-construction artifact with a testable fingerprint, guiding what data (not architecture) to fix.
why_possibly_novel: Causal linking of SA-1B pipeline choices to specific inference-time failure geometry is UNVERIFIED - needs lit search.
minimal_experiment: Compute shape-statistic histograms of SA-1B (public) vs OpenImages/ADE masks; regress SAM failure rate per shape bin against representation gap.
main_risk: Correlation not causation; a small targeted fine-tune on synthetic wiry masks would be needed for the causal leg.

one_liner: At high JPEG compression, SAM boundaries snap to 8x8 block-grid artifacts; quantify compression-boundary coupling.
problem: Deployment images are heavily compressed; block artifacts create fake edges aligned to a fixed grid. Whether promptable models lock onto them is untested.
core_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: as JPEG quality decreases, the phase histogram of SAM boundary positions modulo 8 px develops peaks at block boundaries, and this grid-snapping accounts for a measurable share of the compression-induced IoU drop.
why_important: A concrete, correctable deployment failure (choose compression settings / add dither) with a clean forensic signature.
why_possibly_novel: Compression robustness is studied as an aggregate score; the grid-phase forensic analysis of boundary placement appears new. UNVERIFIED - needs lit search.
minimal_experiment: Sweep JPEG quality on COCO, compute boundary-position phase histograms and IoU deltas; test dithered decompression as mitigation.
main_risk: Modern webp/HEIC pipelines differ; scope must include them to stay relevant.

one_liner: Test compositionality of SAM's image embedding: does masked-object feature subtraction behave algebraically?
problem: SAM's encoder embedding is treated as a black box. Whether object presence is encoded additively (removable by subtraction, movable by translation in feature space) is unknown.
core_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: SAM embeddings are NOT compositional - subtracting the pooled feature of an object region does not suppress its segmentability, showing objectness is encoded relationally rather than additively (falsifiable: if subtraction works, hypothesis is dead).
why_important: Determines whether feature-space editing (fast object removal, counterfactual segmentation) is possible without pixel-space editing, and probes the representation's algebra.
why_possibly_novel: Feature-arithmetic tests are common for word/CLIP embeddings, rare for dense promptable encoders. UNVERIFIED - needs lit search.
minimal_experiment: For 500 objects: embed image, ablate object features (zero/subtract/shuffle), re-run decoder with same prompt, measure mask persistence.
main_risk: Decoder may re-hallucinate objects from context, confounding 'representation holds object' with 'decoder guesses'.

one_liner: Grid-prompted 'segment everything' mode has a recall geometry: elongated and off-grid objects are systematically missed as a function of grid density.
problem: Everything-mode uses a regular point grid + NMS; its recall is assumed to rise smoothly with density, but object geometry interacts with the grid non-uniformly.
core_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: at fixed grid density, per-object recall is predicted by the probability that a grid point lands in the object's 'promptable core' (a computable region smaller than the mask), so everything-mode recall can be forecast per dataset without running the model, and elongated objects need quadratically denser grids.
why_important: Everything-mode underlies many auto-annotation pipelines; a predictive recall law would let people budget grid density instead of guessing.
why_possibly_novel: Treats prompt-grid coverage as a geometric sampling problem with a testable analytic form. UNVERIFIED - needs lit search.
minimal_experiment: Estimate promptable cores on 1k objects (dense prompting), derive predicted recall vs grid density, verify against actual everything-mode runs.
main_risk: NMS interactions between neighboring objects may break the independent-coverage approximation.

one_liner: Disagreement among SAM's three heads beats its predicted-IoU score as an out-of-distribution failure detector.
problem: Pipelines filter SAM outputs by predicted IoU, but that head was trained in-distribution and may be blind to OOD failure; the multimask heads provide a free ensemble signal.
core_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: inter-head mask disagreement (pairwise IoU among the 3 outputs) is a better OOD failure predictor than predicted IoU on shifted domains (medical, thermal, art), with the gap growing with shift severity.
why_important: A zero-cost reliability signal for the most common filtering decision in SAM pipelines.
why_possibly_novel: Using ambiguity-head disagreement specifically as an OOD detector, benchmarked against the IoU head, is UNVERIFIED - needs lit search.
minimal_experiment: On 5 shifted datasets with GT, compute AUROC of both signals for predicting IoU<0.5; one GPU-day.
main_risk: Both signals may fail together on strong shift, leaving no winner (still a useful negative result).

one_liner: The Jacobian of SAM's mask w.r.t. prompt location is a label-free edge/structure detector - characterize what it computes.
problem: Differentiating mask output with respect to prompt coordinates yields a sensitivity field over the image. What classical quantity this field approximates (edges, medial axis, affordance boundaries) is unknown.
core_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: the prompt-Jacobian field concentrates on object-ownership boundaries rather than photometric edges, so it matches human-annotated occlusion/ownership boundaries (BSDS-style) better than Canny or learned edge detectors that use photometry alone.
why_important: Would extract a new dense output (boundary ownership) from a frozen model for free, and reveal what geometric structure prompt conditioning learned.
why_possibly_novel: Prompt-space differentiation as a readout mechanism appears unexplored. UNVERIFIED - needs lit search.
minimal_experiment: Finite-difference the prompt over a coarse grid on BSDS500 images, evaluate against boundary GT vs Canny/HED baselines.
main_risk: Field may be too noisy at feasible grid resolutions; smoothing may destroy the claimed specificity.

one_liner: A dataset-level 'promptability score' measured on unlabeled images predicts downstream annotation cost and model fine-tuning difficulty.
problem: Teams choose datasets/domains to annotate with no quantitative predictor of how much SAM-assisted annotation will actually save.
core_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: an unlabeled-data statistic built from SAM behavior (jitter stability, head agreement, everything-mode mask density entropy) predicts realized human correction time per image with r>0.7 across domains, enabling annotation budgeting before any labeling starts.
why_important: Converts anecdotal 'SAM works/doesn't work on our data' into a forecastable quantity with direct economic value.
why_possibly_novel: Dataset-level meta-prediction of assisted-annotation cost is UNVERIFIED - needs lit search.
minimal_experiment: Across 8 public datasets with known annotation protocols, compute the score and correlate with measured correction effort on 50 images each.
main_risk: Ground-truth 'annotation cost' is hard to standardize across domains; needs a controlled labeling study.

one_liner: SAM has an orientation anisotropy: elongated vertical vs horizontal objects segment differently, inherited from photo statistics.
problem: Natural photo datasets have anisotropic orientation statistics (gravity, horizons). Whether promptable segmenters are measurably anisotropic - and whether that transfers as failure on rotated/aerial imagery - is untested.
core_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: SAM IoU on matched elongated objects differs by orientation (e.g. worse for diagonal orientations), the anisotropy profile mirrors SA-1B orientation statistics, and it predicts a large share of SAM's aerial/rotated-image degradation.
why_important: Aerial, microscopy, and document images have no canonical orientation; an inherited gravity prior would be a systematic transfer failure with a cheap fix (orientation TTA).
why_possibly_novel: Orientation-anisotropy audits exist for CN classifiers; for promptable segmentation with a data-statistics linkage, UNVERIFIED - needs lit search.
minimal_experiment: Rotate a fixed object set through 24 angles (with anti-aliased resampling controls), plot IoU vs angle; compare with SA-1B mask orientation histogram.
main_risk: Resampling artifacts can masquerade as model anisotropy; controls must be strict.

one_liner: SAM is biased toward simply-connected masks: objects with holes get their holes filled, at a rate predictable from training statistics.
problem: Donut-topology objects (mugs seen through handles, rings, fences around gaps) require genus>0 masks. Whether promptable models can express and choose them is unquantified.
core_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: SAM fills genus>0 regions at a high rate even when photometric evidence for the hole is strong, and the fill rate tracks the (near-zero) frequency of holed masks in SA-1B - an expressivity-through-data limitation, falsifiable by fine-tuning on synthetic holed masks and watching the rate drop.
why_important: Topology errors corrupt measurement applications (porosity, occlusion reasoning) and are invisible in IoU at small hole sizes.
why_possibly_novel: Genus-statistics audit linking training-mask topology to inference topology bias is UNVERIFIED - needs lit search.
minimal_experiment: Curate 300 holed-object images, measure hole preservation vs hole size/contrast; count genus>0 masks in SA-1B sample for the comparison.
main_risk: Annotated GT for holes is scarce; may need manual curation effort.
